sources.exact_use: EffectiveAlgebraicOddFibre and Lemmas BoundedCanonicalPolynomial, EffectiveFiniteReciprocalBox, ExplicitReciprocalTwistBox and RationalOrbitReduction; universal termination is a written argument, not a finite test.

Explicit rational bounded generator searches, the complete 100-vector no-generator box, asymmetric maximum-ramification pole bounds, full-jet quotient matrices and a number-field restriction-of-scalars control.

Exact marked-curve reciprocity, finite-pole bounds, finite support, canonical cyclic polynomial unit, descent of its geometric generator, all rational reciprocal units in K(R), and the full polynomial jet congruence. The old non-effective Dickson step is replaced here.

Chonev-Ouaknine-Worrell, Theorem 2.2, printed page 0:3: only the one-dimensional-target PTIME clause for the rational-matrix Orbit Problem. Sections 3-4, printed pages 0:5-0:9, include the repeated-eigenvalue equations. Last-coordinate augmentation is proved in the new note; no higher-target or Skolem decision theorem is imported.

primary_source.authors: Ventsislav Chonev, Joel Ouaknine and James Worrell
primary_source.publication: On the Complexity of the Orbit Problem, Journal of the ACM 63(3), Article 23 (2016)
primary_source.edition: Retained 40-page author manuscript; actual Theorem 2.2 and relevant Sections 3-4 inspected
primary_source.imported_scope: Arbitrary rational square matrix and rational initial vector; decide whether its nonnegative orbit meets a one-dimensional rational target subspace. Repeated eigenvalues are allowed.

internal_review.checker_author: The same Jacobian/Dixmier audit agent implemented the finite controls in this packet; this is not an independent replay by that agent.

self_contained_steps: Zeros of the canonical polynomial lie over the opposite infinity value, and its degree divides the rational-map degree.
Absence of a polynomial reciprocal unit makes the exponent polyhedron bounded; the Cramer bound gives a finite explicit box.
Maximum ramification gives the sharp pole-twist intervals before the jet test.
Complete quotient-algebra vectors retain all jets; restriction of scalars and a last coordinate reduce equality to a rational target line.
After an imported positive decision, exact sequential search finds the least exponent; the finite-order test gives the entire integer coset.
